\n(b) shall carry out any process that the Director does not assign to another \nagency (or agencies) under subsection (a); \n(c) may, after consultation with the Secretary of State, Secretary of Defense, \nthe Attorney General, the Secretary of Energy, the Secretary of Homeland \nSecurity, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), and the Director of \nthe Office of Personnel Management, issue guidelines and instructions to \nthe heads of agencies to ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, effi-\nciency, effectiveness, and timeliness in processes relating to determinations \nby agencies of eligibility for access to classified national security information; \n(d) may, with regard to determining eligibility for access to Sensitive \nCompartmented Information (SCI) and ‘‘special access programs pertaining \nto intelligence activities; including special activities, but not including mili-\ntary operational, strategic, and tactical programs’’ (Intelligence SAPs) under \nsection 4.3(a) of Executive Order 12958 of April 17, 1995, as amended, \nissue guidelines and instructions with the concurrence of the DNI to the \nheads of agencies to ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, \neffectiveness, and timeliness in making such determinations relating to those \nprograms; \n(e) may, with regard to determining eligibility for access to special access \nprograms (SAP) as defined in Executive Order 12958 other than Intelligence \nSAPs, issue guidelines and instructions with the concurrence of the agency \nhead with responsibility for the SAP to ensure appropriate uniformity, cen-\ntralization, efficiency, effectiveness, and timeliness in making such deter-\nminations relating to those programs; \n(f) may report periodically to the President on implementation by agencies \nof the policy set forth in section 1; and \nVerDate jul<14>2003 16:49 Jun 29, 2005 Jkt 205001 PO 00000 Frm 00003 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\30JNE0.SGM 30JNE0\n=== PDF page 2 of 3 ===\n37954 Federal Register / Vol. 70, No. 125 / Thursday, June 30, 2005 / Presidential Documents \n(g) shall submit reports to the Congress relating to the subject matter \nof this order to the extent required by law."},{"char_end":7519,"char_start":5761,"text":"(b) the term ‘‘classified national security information ’’ means information \nthat is classified pursuant to Executive Order 12958; \n(c) the term ‘‘counterintelligence’’ has the meaning specified for that term \nin section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 401a); and \n(d) the term ‘‘process’’ means: (i) oversight of determinations of eligibility \nfor access to classified national security information, including for SCI and \nSAPs made by any agency, as well as the acquisition of information through \ninvestigation or other means upon which such determinations are made; \n(ii) developing and implementing uniform and consistent policies and proce-\ndures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of access \neligibility determinations, to include for SAPs; (iii) designating an authorized \nagency for making access eligibility determinations and an authorized agency \nfor collecting information through investigation upon which such determina-\ntions are made; (iv) ensuring reciprocal recognition of determinations of \neligibility for access to classified information among the agencies of the \nUnited States Government, including resolution of disputes involving the \nreciprocity of security clearances and access to SCI and SAPs; (v) ensuring \nthe availability of resources to achieve clearance and investigative program \ngoals regarding the making of access determinations as well as the collection \nof information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made; and (vi) developing tools and techniques for en-\nhancing the making of access eligibility determinations as well as the collec-\ntion of information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made."},{"char_end":9157,"char_start":8864,"text":"(d) Existing delegations of authority to any agency relating to granting \naccess to classified information and conducting investigations shall remain \nin effect, subject to the authority of the Office of Management and Budget \nunder section 2 of this order to revise or revoke such delegation."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10865>EO:13381@6bfaa327153f38ef","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 5.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"whole","signing_date":"2005-06-27","target_id":"EO:10865","verb":"supersede"}
  Text: [T1d1c52a0af1c5827b21ada0c](#t1d1c52a0af1c5827b21ada0c); absolute characters 7549–8336
- **ACT:EO:10865>EO:13381@b7a22866090d00a3**; S4efc7cac0b15916777c7e305; {"actor_id":"EO:13381","char_end":8941,"char_start":8154,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":1469,"char_start":1102,"text":"To the extent consistent with safeguarding the security \nof the United States and protecting classified national security information \nfrom unauthorized disclosure, agency functions relating to determining eligi-\nbility for access to classified national security information shall be appro-\npriately uniform, centralized, efficient, effective, timely, and reciprocal."},{"char_end":4300,"char_start":1529,"text":"The Director \nof the Office of Management and Budget (Director): \n(a) may, to ensure the effective implementation of the policy set forth \nin section 1 of this order, assign, in whole or in part, to the head of \nany agency (solely or jointly) any process relating to determinations of \neligibility for access to classified national security information, with the \nagency’s exercise of such assigned process to be subject to the Director’s \nsupervision and to such terms and conditions (including approval by the \nOffice of Management and Budget) as the Director determines appropriate; \n(b) shall carry out any process that the Director does not assign to another \nagency (or agencies) under subsection (a); \n(c) may, after consultation with the Secretary of State, Secretary of Defense, \nthe Attorney General, the Secretary of Energy, the Secretary of Homeland \nSecurity, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), and the Director of \nthe Office of Personnel Management, issue guidelines and instructions to \nthe heads of agencies to ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, effi-\nciency, effectiveness, and timeliness in processes relating to determinations \nby agencies of eligibility for access to classified national security information; \n(d) may, with regard to determining eligibility for access to Sensitive \nCompartmented Information (SCI) and ‘‘special access programs pertaining \nto intelligence activities; including special activities, but not including mili-\ntary operational, strategic, and tactical programs’’ (Intelligence SAPs) under \nsection 4.3(a) of Executive Order 12958 of April 17, 1995, as amended, \nissue guidelines and instructions with the concurrence of the DNI to the \nheads of agencies to ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, \neffectiveness, and timeliness in making such determinations relating to those \nprograms; \n(e) may, with regard to determining eligibility for access to special access \nprograms (SAP) as defined in Executive Order 12958 other than Intelligence \nSAPs, issue guidelines and instructions with the concurrence of the agency \nhead with responsibility for the SAP to ensure appropriate uniformity, cen-\ntralization, efficiency, effectiveness, and timeliness in making such deter-\nminations relating to those programs; \n(f) may report periodically to the President on implementation by agencies \nof the policy set forth in section 1; and \nVerDate jul<14>2003 16:49 Jun 29, 2005 Jkt 205001 PO 00000 Frm 00003 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\30JNE0.SGM 30JNE0\n=== PDF page 2 of 3 ===\n37954 Federal Register / Vol. 70, No. 125 / Thursday, June 30, 2005 / Presidential Documents \n(g) shall submit reports to the Congress relating to the subject matter \nof this order to the extent required by law."},{"char_end":8124,"char_start":6366,"text":"(b) the term ‘‘classified national security information ’’ means information \nthat is classified pursuant to Executive Order 12958; \n(c) the term ‘‘counterintelligence’’ has the meaning specified for that term \nin section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 401a); and \n(d) the term ‘‘process’’ means: (i) oversight of determinations of eligibility \nfor access to classified national security information, including for SCI and \nSAPs made by any agency, as well as the acquisition of information through \ninvestigation or other means upon which such determinations are made; \n(ii) developing and implementing uniform and consistent policies and proce-\ndures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of access \neligibility determinations, to include for SAPs; (iii) designating an authorized \nagency for making access eligibility determinations and an authorized agency \nfor collecting information through investigation upon which such determina-\ntions are made; (iv) ensuring reciprocal recognition of determinations of \neligibility for access to classified information among the agencies of the \nUnited States Government, including resolution of disputes involving the \nreciprocity of security clearances and access to SCI and SAPs; (v) ensuring \nthe availability of resources to achieve clearance and investigative program \ngoals regarding the making of access determinations as well as the collection \nof information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made; and (vi) developing tools and techniques for en-\nhancing the making of access eligibility determinations as well as the collec-\ntion of information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made."},{"char_end":9762,"char_start":9469,"text":"(d) Existing delegations of authority to any agency relating to granting \naccess to classified information and conducting investigations shall remain \nin effect, subject to the authority of the Office of Management and Budget \nunder section 2 of this order to revise or revoke such delegation."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10865>EO:13381@b7a22866090d00a3","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted.   Text: [Tcd9b054b1ff7725d052f70e7](#tcd9b054b1ff7725d052f70e7); absolute characters 8154–8941
- **ACT:EO:10865>EO:13467**; S023de79d8eb490afcb428b20; {"actor_id":"EO:13467","char_end":17853,"char_start":17312,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":1951,"char_start":1347,"text":"Executive branch policies and procedures relating to \nsuitability, contractor employee fitness, eligibility to hold a sensitive position, \naccess to federally controlled facilities and information systems, and eligi-\nbility for access to classified information shall be aligned using consistent \nstandards to the extent possible, provide for reciprocal recognition, and \nshall ensure cost-effective, timely,and efficient protection of the national \ninterest, while providing fair treatment to those upon whom the Federal \nGovernment relies to conduct our Nation’s business and protect national \nsecurity."},{"char_end":8369,"char_start":7558,"text":"(b) The aligned system shall employ updated and consistent standards and \nmethods, enable innovations with enterprise information technology capabili-\nties and end-to-end automation to the extent practicable, and ensure that \nrelevant information maintained by agencies can be accessed and shared \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 18:32 Jul 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00004 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\02JYE0.SGM 02JYE0hsrobinson on PROD1PC76 with PROPOSALS2\n=== PDF page 3 of 6 ===\n38105 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 128 / Wednesday, July 2, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nrapidly across the executive branch, while protecting national security, pro-\ntecting privacy-related information, ensuring resulting decisions are in the \nnational interest, and providing the Federal Government with an effective \nworkforce."},{"char_end":11953,"char_start":11412,"text":"(e) The Chair may, to ensure the effective implementation of the policy \nset forth in section 1.1 of this order and to the extent consistent with \nlaw, assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely or \njointly) any function within the Council ’s responsibility relating to alignment \nand improvement of investigations and determinations of suitability, con-\ntractor employee fitness, eligibility for logical and physical access, eligibility \nfor access to classified information, or eligibility to hold a sensitive position."},{"char_end":12890,"char_start":12501,"text":"As the Suitability Executive Agent, the Director \nof the Office of Personnel Management will continue to be responsible \nfor developing and implementing uniform and consistent policies and proce-\ndures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of investiga-\ntions and adjudications relating to determinations of suitability and eligibility \nfor logical and physical access."},{"char_end":15137,"char_start":12980,"text":"The Security Executive Agent: \n(i) shall direct the oversight of investigations and determinations of eligi-\nbility for access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive \nposition made by any agency; \n(ii) shall be responsible for developing uniform and consistent policies \nand procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion \nof investigations and adjudications relating to determinations of eligibility \nfor access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; \n(iii) may issue guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies to \nensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, effectiveness, and \ntimeliness in processes relating to determinations by agencies of eligibility \nfor access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; \n(iv) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies \nto conduct investigations of persons who are proposed for access to classi-\nfied information to ascertain whether such persons satisfy the criteria \nfor obtaining and retaining access to classified information or eligibility \nto hold a sensitive position; \n(v) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies \nto determine eligibility for access to classified information in accordance \nwith Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995; \n(vi) shall ensure reciprocal recognition of eligibility for access to classified \ninformation among the agencies, including acting as the final authority \nto arbitrate and resolve disputes among the agencies involving the reci-\nprocity of investigations and determinations of eligibility for access to \nclassified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; and \n(vii) may assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely \nor jointly) any of the functions detailed in (i) through (vi), above, with \nthe agency ’s exercise of such assigned functions to be subject to the \nSecurity Executive Agent ’s oversight and with such terms and conditions \n(including approval by the Security Executive Agent) as the Security Execu-\ntive Agent determines appropriate."},{"char_end":20366,"char_start":19744,"text":"VerDate Aug<31>2005 18:32 Jul 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00007 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\02JYE0.SGM 02JYE0hsrobinson on PROD1PC76 with PROPOSALS2\n=== PDF page 6 of 6 ===\n38108 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 128 / Wednesday, July 2, 2008 / Presidential Documents \n(g) Existing delegations of authority made pursuant to Executive Order 13381 \nof June 27, 2005, as amended, to any agency relating to granting eligibility \nfor access to classified information and conducting investigations shall 13 \nremain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities pursuant to this \norder to revise or revoke such delegation."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10865>EO:13467","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 3.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"whole","signing_date":"2008-06-30","target_id":"EO:10865","verb":"supersede"}

Government’s tools, systems, and processes for conducting these \nbackground investigations and managing sensitive investigative information \nshould keep pace with technological advancements, regularly integrating \ncurrent best practices to better anticipate, detect, and counter malicious \nactivities, and threats posed by external or internal actors who may seek \nto do harm to the Government’s personnel, property, and information."},{"char_end":13478,"char_start":12783,"text":"To help fulfill these responsibilities, there shall be a primary executive \nbranch investigative sustained \nby an enhanced risk-management approach that facilitates early detection \nof issues by an informed, aware, and responsible Federal workforce; results \nin quality decisions enabled by improved vetting capabilities; and advances \nGovernment-wide capabilities through enterprise approaches. \n‘‘(d) The appointment or retention of each covered individual shall be \nsubject to an investigation."},{"char_end":23242,"char_start":19592,"text":"It relies on re-\nsearch to generate data-driven decisions and uses outcome-based measure-\nments to adjust policy and operations. \n‘‘(f) an official who has succeeded \nto that office under applicable law in accordance with Executive Order \n13549 of August 18, 2010, and its implementing directive.’’ \n(j) New sections 1.3(k) and 1.3(l) are added to Executive Order 13467 \nto read as follows: \n‘‘(k) ‘Fitness’ means the level of character and conduct determined nec-\nessary for an individual to perform work for or on behalf of a Federal \nagency as an employee in the excepted service (other than a position \nsubject to suitability), or as a ‘contractor employee’ or a ‘nonappropriated \nfund employee’ as those terms are defined in Executive Order 13488 \nof January 16, 2009, as amended. \n‘‘(l) ‘Investigation’ means the collection and analysis of pertinent facts \nand data to support a determination of whether a covered individual \nis, and continues to be: \n‘‘(i) eligible for access to classified information; \n‘‘(ii) eligible to hold a sensitive position; \n‘‘(iii) suitable or fit for Federal employment; \n‘‘(iv) fit to perform work for or on behalf of the Federal Government \nas a contractor or nonappropriated fund employee; or \n‘‘(v) authorized to be issued a Federal credential.’’ \n(k) established within the Office \nof Personnel Management under section 1103(a)(3) of title 5, United States \nCode, or a successor entity, with responsibility for conducting effective, \nefficient, and secure personnel background investigations pursuant to law, \nrule, regulation, or Executive Order.’’ \n(l) Redesignated section 1.3(o) of Executive Order 13467 is revised to \nread as follows: \n‘‘(o) ‘Sensitive Position’ means any position within or in support of a \ndepartment or agency, the occupant of which could bring about, by virtue \nof the nature of the position, a material adverse effect on the national \nsecurity, regardless of whether the occupant has access to classified infor-\nmation, and regardless of whether the occupant is an employee, a military \nservice member, or a contractor."},{"char_end":25955,"char_start":25056,"text":"The Executive Agents shall issue guidance to \nimplement this provision. \n‘‘(b) The aligned executive branch-wide vetting enterprise shall employ \nmodern and consistent standards and methods, enable innovations with \nenterprise information technology capabilities and end-to-end automation \nto the extent practicable, and ensure that relevant information maintained \nby agencies can be accessed and shared rapidly across the executive \nbranch, while protecting national security, protecting privacy-related infor-\nmation, protecting civil rights and civil liberties, ensuring resulting deci-\nsions are in the national interest and in accordance with due process \nrequirements, and providing the Federal Government with an effective \ntrusted workforce. \n‘‘(c) The investigative and adjudicative standards for fitness shall, to the \nextent practicable, be consistent with the standards for position designation requirements with regard \nto the risk to the efficiency and integrity of the service; prescribing applica-\nble investigative standards, policies, and procedures for suitability and \nfitness; prescribing suitability and fitness reciprocity standards; making \nsuitability determinations; and taking suitability actions; \n‘‘(ii) shall issue regulations, guidance, and standards uniformity, centralization, efficiency, effectiveness, \nreciprocity, timeliness, and security in processes relating to determining \nsuitability or fitness; and \n‘‘(vii) shall, pursuant to section Executive branch vetting policies and procedures \nrelating to suitability, contractor or Federal employee fitness, eligibility to \nhold a sensitive position, authorization to be issued a Federal credential \nfor access to federally controlled facilities and information systems, and \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 21:05 Jan 19, 2017 Jkt 241001 PO 00000 Frm 00005 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\23JAE0.SGM 23JAE0asabaliauskas on DSK3SPTVN1PROD with E0\n=== PDF page 4 of 15 ===\n8118 Federal Register / Vol. 82, No. 13 / Monday, January 23, 2017 / Presidential Documents \neligibility for access to classified information shall be aligned using consistent \nstandards to the extent possible, shall provide for reciprocal recognition, \nand shall ensure cost-effective, timely, and efficient protection of the national \ninterest, while providing fair treatment to those upon whom the Federal \nGovernment relies to conduct our Nation’s business and protect national \nsecurity. \n‘‘(b) The Government’s tools, systems, and processes for conducting these \nbackground investigations and managing sensitive investigative information \nshould keep pace with technological advancements, regularly integrating \ncurrent best practices to better anticipate, detect, and counter malicious \nactivities, and threats posed by external or internal actors who may seek \nto do harm to the Government’s personnel, property, and information."},{"char_end":13478,"char_start":12783,"text":"To help fulfill these responsibilities, there shall be a primary executive \nbranch investigative service provider whose mission is to provide effective, \nefficient, and secure background investigations for the Federal Government. \n‘‘(c) Executive branch vetting policies and procedures shall be sustained \nby an enhanced risk-management approach that facilitates early detection \nof issues by an informed, aware, and responsible Federal workforce; results \nin quality decisions enabled by improved vetting capabilities; and advances \nGovernment-wide capabilities through enterprise approaches. \n‘‘(d) The appointment or retention of each covered individual shall be \nsubject to an investigation."},{"char_end":23242,"char_start":19592,"text":"It relies on re-\nsearch to generate data-driven decisions and uses outcome-based measure-\nments to adjust policy and operations. \n‘‘(f) ‘Continuous vetting’ means reviewing the background of a covered \nindividual at any time to determine whether that individual continues \nto meet applicable requirements.’’ \n(i) Redesignated section 1.3(h) of Executive Order 13467 is revised to \nread as follows: \n‘‘(h) ‘Covered individual’ means a person who performs, or who seeks \nto perform, work for or on behalf of the executive branch (e.g., Federal \nemployee, military member, or contractor), or otherwise interacts with \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 21:05 Jan 19, 2017 Jkt 241001 PO 00000 Frm 00007 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\23JAE0.SGM 23JAE0asabaliauskas on DSK3SPTVN1PROD with E0\n=== PDF page 6 of 15 ===\n8120 Federal Register / Vol. 82, No. 13 / Monday, January 23, 2017 / Presidential Documents \nthe executive branch such that the individual must undergo vetting, but \ndoes not include: \n‘‘(i) the President or (except to the extent otherwise directed by the \nPresident) employees of the President under section 105 or 107 of title \n3, United States Code; \n‘‘(ii) the Vice President or (except to the extent otherwise directed \nby the Vice President) employees of the Vice President under section \n106 of title 3, United States Code, or annual legislative branch appropria-\ntions acts; or \n‘‘(iii) with respect to background investigations only, duly elected or \nappointed governor of a State or territory, or an official who has succeeded \nto that office under applicable law in accordance with Executive Order \n13549 of August 18, 2010, and its implementing directive.’’ \n(j) New sections 1.3(k) and 1.3(l) are added to Executive Order 13467 \nto read as follows: \n‘‘(k) ‘Fitness’ means the level of character and conduct determined nec-\nessary for an individual to perform work for or on behalf of a Federal \nagency as an employee in the excepted service (other than a position \nsubject to suitability), or as a ‘contractor employee’ or a ‘nonappropriated \nfund employee’ as those terms are defined in Executive Order 13488 \nof January 16, 2009, as amended. \n‘‘(l) ‘Investigation’ means the collection and analysis of pertinent facts \nand data to support a determination of whether a covered individual \nis, and continues to be: \n‘‘(i) eligible for access to classified information; \n‘‘(ii) eligible to hold a sensitive position; \n‘‘(iii) suitable or fit for Federal employment; \n‘‘(iv) fit to perform work for or on behalf of the Federal Government \nas a contractor or nonappropriated fund employee; or \n‘‘(v) authorized to be issued a Federal credential.’’ \n(k) Redesignated section 1.3(n) of Executive Order 13467 is revised to \nread as follows: \n‘‘(n) ‘National Background Investigations Bureau’ (NBIB) means the Na-\ntional Background Investigations Bureau, established within the Office \nof Personnel Management under section 1103(a)(3) of title 5, United States \nCode, or a successor entity, with responsibility for conducting effective, \nefficient, and secure personnel background investigations pursuant to law, \nrule, regulation, or Executive Order.’’ \n(l) Redesignated section 1.3(o) of Executive Order 13467 is revised to \nread as follows: \n‘‘(o) ‘Sensitive Position’ means any position within or in support of a \ndepartment or agency, the occupant of which could bring about, by virtue \nof the nature of the position, a material adverse effect on the national \nsecurity, regardless of whether the occupant has access to classified infor-\nmation, and regardless of whether the occupant is an employee, a military \nservice member, or a contractor."},{"char_end":25955,"char_start":25056,"text":"The Executive Agents shall issue guidance to \nimplement this provision. \n‘‘(b) The aligned executive branch-wide vetting enterprise shall employ \nmodern and consistent standards and methods, enable innovations with \nenterprise information technology capabilities and end-to-end automation \nto the extent practicable, and ensure that relevant information maintained \nby agencies can be accessed and shared rapidly across the executive \nbranch, while protecting national security, protecting privacy-related infor-\nmation, protecting civil rights and civil liberties, ensuring resulting deci-\nsions are in the national interest and in accordance with due process \nrequirements, and providing the Federal Government with an effective \ntrusted workforce. \n‘‘(c) The investigative and adjudicative standards for fitness shall, to the \nextent practicable, be consistent with the standards for suitability."},{"char_end":40174,"char_start":33491,"text":"With respect to the \nSuitability Executive Agent functions, the Director: \n‘‘(i) shall, pursuant to sections 1103 and 1104 of title 5, United States \nCode, and the Civil Service Rules, be responsible for suitability and fitness \nby prescribing suitability standards and minimum standards of fitness \nfor employment; prescribing position designation requirements with regard \nto the risk to the efficiency and integrity of the service; prescribing applica-\nble investigative standards, policies, and procedures for suitability and \nfitness; prescribing suitability and fitness reciprocity standards; making \nsuitability determinations; and taking suitability actions; \n‘‘(ii) shall issue regulations, guidance, and standards to fulfill the Direc-\ntor’s responsibilities related to suitability and fitness under Executive Order \n13488 of January 16, 2009, as amended; \n‘‘(iii) shall promote reciprocal recognition of suitability or fitness deter-\nminations among the agencies, including acting as the final authority \nto arbitrate and resolve disputes among the agencies involving the reci-\nprocity of investigations and adjudications of suitability and fitness; \n‘‘(iv) shall continue to initially approve, and periodically review for \nrenewal, agencies’ requests to administer polygraphs in connection with \nappointment in the competitive service, in consultation with the Security \nExecutive Agent as appropriate; \n‘‘(v) shall make a continuing review of agency programs for suitability \nand fitness vetting to determine whether they are being implemented \naccording to this order; \n‘‘(vi) may issue guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies \nto promote appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, effectiveness, \nreciprocity, timeliness, and security in processes relating to determining \nsuitability or fitness; and \n‘‘(vii) shall, pursuant to section 1104 of title 5, United States Code, \nprescribe performance standards and a system of oversight for any suit-\nability or fitness function delegated by the Director to the head of another \nagency, including uniform and consistent policies and procedures to ensure \nthe effective, efficient, timely, and secure completion of delegated func-\ntions. \n‘‘(c) With respect to the Credentialing 23JAE0asabaliauskas on DSK3SPTVN1PROD with E0\n=== PDF page 10 of 15 ===\n8124 Federal Register / Vol. 82, No. 13 / Monday, January 23, 2017 / Presidential Documents \n‘‘(i) shall develop standards for investigations, reinvestigations, and con-\ntinuous vetting for a covered individual’s eligibility for a personal identity \nverification credential permitting logical and physical access to federally \ncontrolled facilities and federally controlled information systems (PIV cre-\ndential); \n‘‘(ii) shall develop adjudicative guidelines for a covered individual’s \neligibility for a PIV credential; \n‘‘(iii) shall develop guidelines on reporting and recording determinations \nof eligibility for a PIV credential; \n‘‘(iv) shall develop standards for unfavorable determinations of eligibility \nfor a PIV credential, including procedures for denying and revoking the \neligibility for a PIV credential, for reconsideration of unfavorable deter-\nminations, and for rendering the PIV credential inoperable; \n‘‘(v) shall develop standards and procedures for suspending eligibility \nfor a PIV credential when there is a reasonable basis to believe there \nmay be an unacceptable risk pending an inquiry or investigation, including \nspecial standards and procedures for imminent risk; \n‘‘(vi) shall be responsible for developing uniform and consistent policies \nand procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, and secure comple-\ntion of investigations and adjudications relating to eligibility for a PIV \ncredential; \n‘‘(vii) may develop guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies \nas necessary to ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, \neffectiveness, and timeliness in processes relating to eligibility for a PIV \ncredential; \n‘‘(viii) shall monitor and make a continuing review of agency programs \nfor determining eligibility for a PIV credential to determine whether they \nare being implemented according to this order; and \n‘‘(ix) shall consult to the extent practicable with other agencies with \nresponsibilities related to PIV credentials to ensure that policies and proce-\ndures are consistent with law including: \n‘‘(A) the Office of Management and Budget, in exercising its respon-\nsibilities under section 11331 of title 40, United States Code, section \n3553(a) of title 44, United States exercising its respon-\nsibilities under sections 3553(b), (f), and (g) of title 44, United States \nCode; \n‘‘(C) the Department of Defense, in exercising its responsibilities under \nsection 3553(e) of title 44, United States Code, and division A, sec-\ntions 1086(a)(1)(E), (b)(1), and (b)(2) of Public Law 114–92; \n‘‘(D) the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, in exercising \nits responsibilities under section 3553(e) of title 44, United States \nCode, and division A, section 1086(b)(2) of Public Law 114–92; \n‘‘(E) the Department of Commerce and the National Institute of Stand-\nards and Technology, in exercising their responsibilities under section \n278g–3 of title 15, United States Code, and Homeland Security Presi-\ndential Directive 12 of August 27, 2004; \n‘‘(F) the General Services Administration, in exercising its responsibil-\nities under division A, section 1086(b)(2) of Public Law 114–92; and \n‘‘(G) the Federal Acquisition Regulation agencies, in exercising their \nresponsibilities under chapter 137 of title 10, section 121(c) of title \n40, and section 20113 of title 51, United States Code. \n‘‘(d) In fulfilling the Credentialing Executive Agent function of developing \npolicies and procedures for determining eligibility for a PIV credential \nand to protect the national security, the Director of the Office of Personnel \nManagement Principals."},{"char_end":43787,"char_start":40521,"text":"The Security Executive Agent: \n‘‘(i) shall direct the oversight of investigations, reinvestigations, adjudica-\ntions, and, as applicable, polygraphs for eligibility for access to classified \ninformation or eligibility to hold a sensitive position made by any agency; \n‘‘(ii) shall make a continuing review of agencies’ national security back-\nground investigation and adjudication programs to determine whether they \nare being implemented according to this order; \n‘‘(iii) shall be responsible for developing and issuing uniform and con-\nsistent policies and procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, \nand secure completion of investigations, polygraphs, and adjudications \nrelating to determinations of eligibility for access to classified information \nor eligibility to hold a sensitive position; \n‘‘(iv) may issue guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies \nto ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, effectiveness, \ntimeliness, and security in processes relating to determinations by agencies \nof eligibility for access to classified information or eligibility to hold \na sensitive position, to include such matters as investigations, polygraphs, \nadjudications, and reciprocity; \n‘‘(v) may, if consistent with the national security, authorize exceptions \nto or waivers of national security investigative requirements, and may \nissue implementing or clarifying guidance as necessary; \n‘‘(vi) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies, \nto the extent that it is not practicable to use the National Background \nInvestigations Bureau, to conduct investigations of persons who are pro-\nposed for access to classified information or for eligibility to hold a sen-\nsitive position to ascertain whether such persons satisfy the criteria for \nobtaining and retaining access to classified information or eligibility to \nhold a sensitive position; \n‘‘(vii) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies \nto determine eligibility for access to classified information or eligibility \nto hold a sensitive position in accordance with Executive Order 12968 \nof August 2, 1995, as amended; \n‘‘(viii) shall ensure reciprocal recognition of eligibility for access to \nclassified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position among \nthe agencies, including acting as the final authority to arbitrate and resolve \ndisputes among the agencies involving the reciprocity of investigations \nand adjudications of eligibility; and \n‘‘(ix) may assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely \nor jointly) any of the functions detailed in (i) through (viii) of this sub-\nsection, with the agency’s exercise of such assigned functions to be subject \nto the Security Executive Agent’s oversight and with such terms and \nconditions (including approval by the Security Executive Agent) as the \nSecurity Executive Agent determines appropriate. \n‘‘(f) Nothing in this section shall be construed in a manner that would \nlimit the authorities of the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, \nthe Director of National Intelligence, or the Secretary of Defense under \nlaw.’’ \n(t) Redesignated section 2.6 of Executive Order 13467 is revised to read \nas follows: \n‘‘Sec. 2.6."},{"char_end":46485,"char_start":43788,"text":"Roles and Responsibilities of the National Background Investiga-\ntions Bureau and the Department of Defense. \n‘‘(a) The National E0\n=== PDF page 12 of 15 ===\n8126 Federal Register / Vol. 82, No. 13 / Monday, January 23, 2017 / Presidential Documents \n‘‘(1) serve as the primary executive branch service provider for back-\nground investigations for eligibility for access to classified information; \neligibility to hold a sensitive position; suitability or, for employees in \npositions not subject to suitability, fitness for Government employment; \nfitness to perform work for or on behalf of the Government as a contractor; \nfitness to work as a nonappropriated fund employee, as defined in Execu-\ntive Order 13488 of January 16, 2009, as amended; and authorization \nto be issued a Federal credential for logical and physical access to federally \ncontrolled facilities or information systems; \n‘‘(2) provide effective, efficient, and secure personnel background inves-\ntigations for the Federal Government; \n‘‘(3) provide the Council information, to the extent permitted by law, \non matters of performance, timeliness, capacity, information technology \nmodernization, continuous performance improvement, and other relevant \naspects of NBIB operations; \n‘‘(4) be headquartered in or near Washington, District of Columbia; \n‘‘(5) have dedicated resources, including but not limited to a senior \nprivacy and civil liberties official; \n‘‘(6) institutionalize interagency collaboration and leverage expertise \nacross the executive branch; \n‘‘(7) continuously improve investigative operations, emphasizing infor-\nmation accuracy and protection, and regularly integrate best practices, \nincluding those identified by subject matter experts from industry, aca-\ndemia, or other relevant sources; \n‘‘(8) conduct personnel background investigations in accordance with \nuniform and consistent policies, procedures, standards, and requirements \nestablished by the Security Executive Agent and the Suitability and \nCredentialing Executive Agent exercising its Suitability Executive Agent \nfunctions; and \n‘‘(9) conduct other personnel background investigations as authorized \nby law, rule, regulation, or Executive Order.’’ \n‘‘(b) The Secretary of Defense shall design, develop, deploy, operate, secure, \ndefend, and continuously update and modernize, as necessary, vetting \ninformation technology systems that support all background investigation \nprocesses conducted by the National Background Investigations Bureau."},{"char_end":47559,"char_start":46801,"text":"The Secretary of Defense shall operate the data-\nbase in the information technology systems containing appropriate data \nrelevant to the granting, denial, or revocation of eligibility for access \nto classified information or eligibility for a sensitive position pertaining \nto military, civilian, or Government contractor personnel, see section \n3341(e) of title 50, United States Code, consistent with and following \nan explicit delegation from the Director of the Office of Personnel Manage-\nment pursuant to section 1104 of title 5, United States Code.’’ \n‘‘(c) Delegations and designations of investigative authority in place on \nthe date of establishment of the National Background Investigations Bureau \nshall remain in effect until amended or revoked."},{"char_end":50558,"char_start":48068,"text":"The Council shall hold the National Background \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 Subsections (b) and (c) of redesignated section 2.7 of Executive Order \n13467 are revised to read as follows: \n‘‘(b) Heads of agencies shall: \n‘‘(i) designate, or cause to be designated, as a ‘sensitive position,’ any \nposition occupied by a covered individual in which the occupant could \nbring about by virtue of the nature of the position, a material adverse \neffect on the national security; \n‘‘(ii) establish and maintain within their respective agencies, an effective \nprogram to ensure that employment and retention of any covered individual \nwithin the agency is clearly consistent with the interests of national security \nand, as applicable, meets standards for eligibility for access to classified \ninformation or to hold a sensitive position, suitability, fitness, or \ncredentialing, established by the respective Executive Agent; \n‘‘(iii) carry out any function assigned to the agency head by the Chair, \nand shall assist the Chair, the Council, the Executive Agents, the National \nBackground Investigations Bureau, and the Department of Defense in car-\nrying out any function under sections 2.4, 2.5, and 2.6 of this order; \n‘‘(iv) implement any policy or procedure established pursuant to this \norder; \n‘‘(v) to the extent permitted by law, make available to the Council, \nthe Executive Agents, the National Background Investigations Bureau, and \nthe Department of Defense such information as may be requested to imple-\nment this order, including information necessary to implement enterprise- \nwide vetting policies and procedures; \n‘‘(vi) except as authorized by section 3341(e)(5) of title 50, United States \nCode, promptly furnish, or cause to be promptly furnished, to the Office \nof Personnel Management the information deemed by the Executive Agents \nto be necessary for purposes of record keeping and reciprocity including, \nbut not limited to, the date on which a background investigation is initiated, \nthe date on which the connection with \nappointment in the competitive service, in consultation with the Security \nExecutive Agent as appropriate; \n‘‘(v) shall make a continuing review of agency programs for suitability \nand fitness vetting to determine whether they are being implemented \naccording to this order; \n‘‘(vi) may issue guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies \nto promote appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, effectiveness, \nreciprocity, timeliness, and security in processes relating to determining \nsuitability or fitness; and \n‘‘(vii) shall, pursuant to section 1104 of title 5, United States Code, \nprescribe performance standards and a system of oversight for any suit-\nability or fitness function delegated by the Director to the head of another \nagency, including uniform and consistent policies and procedures to ensure \nthe effective, efficient, timely, and secure completion of delegated func-\ntions. \n‘‘(c) With respect to the Credentialing 23JAE0asabaliauskas on DSK3SPTVN1PROD with E0\n=== PDF page 10 of 15 ===\n8124 Federal Register / Vol. 82, No. 13 / Monday, January 23, 2017 / Presidential Documents \n‘‘(i) shall develop standards for investigations, reinvestigations, and con-\ntinuous vetting for a covered individual’s eligibility for a personal identity \nverification credential permitting logical and physical access to federally \ncontrolled facilities and federally controlled information systems (PIV cre-\ndential); \n‘‘(ii) shall develop adjudicative guidelines for a covered individual’s \neligibility for a PIV credential; \n‘‘(iii) shall develop guidelines on reporting and recording determinations \nof eligibility for a PIV credential; \n‘‘(iv) shall develop standards for unfavorable determinations of eligibility \nfor a PIV credential, including procedures for denying and revoking the \neligibility for a PIV credential, for reconsideration of unfavorable deter-\nminations, and for rendering the PIV credential inoperable; \n‘‘(v) shall develop standards and procedures for suspending eligibility \nfor a PIV credential when there is a reasonable basis to believe there \nmay be an unacceptable risk pending an inquiry or investigation, including \nspecial standards and procedures for imminent risk; \n‘‘(vi) shall be responsible for developing uniform and consistent policies \nand procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, and secure comple-\ntion of investigations and adjudications relating to eligibility for a PIV \ncredential; \n‘‘(vii) may develop guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies \nas necessary to ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, \neffectiveness, and timeliness in processes relating to eligibility for a PIV \ncredential; \n‘‘(viii) shall monitor and make a continuing review of agency programs \nfor determining eligibility for a PIV credential to determine whether they \nare being implemented according to this order; and \n‘‘(ix) shall consult to the extent practicable with other agencies with \nresponsibilities related to PIV credentials to ensure that policies and proce-\ndures are consistent with law including: \n‘‘(A) the Office of Management and Budget, in exercising its respon-\nsibilities under section 11331 of title 40, United States Code, section \n3553(a) of title 44, United States of title 44, United States Code, and division A, sec-\ntions 1086(a)(1)(E), (b)(1), and (b)(2) of Public Law 114–92; \n‘‘(D) the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, in exercising \nits responsibilities under section 3553(e) of title 44, United States \nCode, and division A, section 1086(b)(2) of Public Law 114–92; \n‘‘(E) the Department of Commerce and the National Institute of Stand-\nards and Technology, in exercising their responsibilities under section \n278g–3 of title 15, United States Code, and Homeland Security Presi-\ndential Directive 12 of August 27, 2004; \n‘‘(F) the General Services Administration, in exercising its responsibil-\nities under division A, section 1086(b)(2) of Public Law 114–92; and \n‘‘(G) the Federal Acquisition Regulation agencies, in exercising their \nresponsibilities under chapter 137 of title 10, section 121(c) of title \n40, and section 20113 of title 51, United States Code. \n‘‘(d) In fulfilling the Credentialing Executive Agent function of developing \npolicies and procedures for determining eligibility for a PIV credential \nand to protect the national security, the Director of the Office of Personnel \nManagement shall coordinate with and obtain the concurrence of the \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 21:05 Jan 19, 2017 Jkt 241001 PO 00000 Frm 00012 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\23JAE0.SGM 23JAE0asabaliauskas on Principals."},{"char_end":43177,"char_start":39911,"text":"The Security Executive Agent: \n‘‘(i) shall direct the oversight of investigations, reinvestigations, adjudica-\ntions, and, as applicable, polygraphs for eligibility for access to classified \ninformation or eligibility to hold a sensitive position made by any agency; \n‘‘(ii) shall make a continuing review of agencies’ national security back-\nground investigation and adjudication programs to determine whether they \nare being implemented according to this order; \n‘‘(iii) shall be responsible for developing and issuing uniform and con-\nsistent policies and procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, \nand secure completion of investigations, polygraphs, and adjudications \nrelating to determinations of eligibility for access to classified information \nor eligibility to hold a sensitive position; \n‘‘(iv) may issue guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies \nto ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, effectiveness, \ntimeliness, and security in processes relating to determinations by agencies \nof eligibility for access to classified information or eligibility to hold \na sensitive position, to include such matters as investigations, polygraphs, \nadjudications, and reciprocity; \n‘‘(v) may, if consistent with the national security, authorize exceptions \nto or waivers of national security investigative requirements, and may \nissue implementing or clarifying guidance as necessary; \n‘‘(vi) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies, \nto the extent that it is not practicable to use the National Background \nInvestigations Bureau, to conduct investigations of persons who are pro-\nposed for access to classified information or for eligibility to hold a sen-\nsitive position to ascertain whether such persons satisfy the criteria for \nobtaining and retaining access to classified information or eligibility to \nhold a sensitive position; \n‘‘(vii) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies \nto determine eligibility for access to classified information or eligibility \nto hold a sensitive position in accordance with Executive Order 12968 \nof August 2, 1995, as amended; \n‘‘(viii) shall ensure reciprocal recognition of eligibility for access to \nclassified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position among \nthe agencies, including acting as the final authority to arbitrate and resolve \ndisputes among the agencies involving the reciprocity of investigations \nand adjudications of eligibility; and \n‘‘(ix) may assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely \nor jointly) any of the functions detailed in (i) through (viii) of this sub-\nsection, with the agency’s exercise of such assigned functions to be subject \nto the Security Executive Agent’s oversight and with such terms and \nconditions (including approval by the Security Executive Agent) as the \nSecurity Executive Agent determines appropriate. \n‘‘(f) Nothing in this section shall be construed in a manner that would \nlimit the authorities of the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, \nthe Director of National Intelligence, or the Secretary of Defense under \nlaw.’’ \n(t) Redesignated section 2.6 of Executive Order 13467 is revised to read \nas follows: \n‘‘Sec. 2.6."},{"char_end":45875,"char_start":43178,"text":"Roles and Responsibilities of the National Background Investiga-\ntions Bureau and the Department of Defense. \n‘‘(a) The National E0\n=== PDF page 12 of 15 ===\n8126 Federal Register / Vol. 82, No. 13 / Monday, January 23, 2017 / Presidential Documents \n‘‘(1) serve as the primary executive branch service provider for back-\nground investigations for eligibility for access to classified information; \neligibility to hold a sensitive position; suitability or, for employees in \npositions not subject to suitability, fitness for Government employment; \nfitness to perform work for or on behalf of the Government as a contractor; \nfitness to work as a nonappropriated fund employee, as defined in Execu-\ntive Order 13488 of January 16, 2009, as amended; and authorization \nto be issued a Federal credential for logical and physical access to federally \ncontrolled facilities or information systems; \n‘‘(2) provide effective, efficient, and secure personnel background inves-\ntigations for the Federal Government; \n‘‘(3) provide the Council information, to the extent permitted by law, \non matters of performance, timeliness, capacity, information technology \nmodernization, continuous performance improvement, and other relevant \naspects of NBIB operations; \n‘‘(4) be headquartered in or near Washington, District of Columbia; \n‘‘(5) have dedicated resources, including but not limited to a senior \nprivacy and civil liberties official; \n‘‘(6) institutionalize interagency collaboration and leverage expertise \nacross the executive branch; \n‘‘(7) continuously improve investigative operations, emphasizing infor-\nmation accuracy and protection, and regularly integrate best practices, \nincluding those identified by subject matter experts from industry, aca-\ndemia, or other relevant sources; \n‘‘(8) conduct personnel background investigations in accordance with \nuniform and consistent policies, procedures, standards, and requirements \nestablished by the Security Executive Agent and the Suitability and \nCredentialing Executive Agent exercising its Suitability Executive Agent \nfunctions; and \n‘‘(9) conduct other personnel background investigations as authorized \nby law, rule, regulation, or Executive Order.’’ \n‘‘(b) The Secretary of Defense shall design, develop, deploy, operate, secure, \ndefend, and continuously update and modernize, as necessary, vetting \ninformation technology systems that support all background investigation \nprocesses conducted by the National Background Investigations Bureau."},{"char_end":46949,"char_start":46191,"text":"The Secretary of Defense shall operate the data-\nbase in the information technology systems containing appropriate data \nrelevant to the granting, denial, or revocation of eligibility for access \nto classified information or eligibility for a sensitive position pertaining \nto military, civilian, or Government contractor personnel, see section \n3341(e) of title 50, United States Code, consistent with and following \nan explicit delegation from the Director of the Office of Personnel Manage-\nment pursuant to section 1104 of title 5, United States Code.’’ \n‘‘(c) Delegations and designations of investigative authority in place on \nthe date of establishment of the National Background Investigations Bureau \nshall remain in effect until amended or revoked."},{"char_end":49948,"char_start":47458,"text":"The Council shall hold the National Background \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 ‘sensitive position,’ any \nposition occupied by a covered individual in which the occupant could \nbring about by virtue of the nature of the position, a material adverse \neffect on the national security; \n‘‘(ii) establish and maintain within their respective agencies, an effective \nprogram to ensure that employment and retention of any covered individual \nwithin the agency is clearly consistent with the interests of national security \nand, as applicable, meets standards for eligibility for access to classified \ninformation or to hold a sensitive position, suitability, fitness, or \ncredentialing, established by the respective Executive Agent; \n‘‘(iii) carry out any function assigned to the agency head by the Chair, \nand shall assist the Chair, the Council, the Executive Agents, the National \nBackground Investigations Bureau, and the Department of Defense in car-\nrying out any function under sections 2.4, 2.5, and 2.6 of this order; \n‘‘(iv) implement any policy or procedure established pursuant to this \norder; \n‘‘(v) to the extent permitted by law, make available to the Council, \nthe Executive Agents, the National Background Investigations Bureau, and \nthe Department of Defense such information as may be requested to imple-\nment this order, including information necessary to implement enterprise- \nwide vetting policies and procedures; \n‘‘(vi) except as authorized by section 3341(e)(5) of title 50, United States \nCode, promptly furnish, or cause to be promptly furnished, to the Office \nof Personnel Management the information deemed by the Executive Agents \nto be necessary for purposes of record keeping and reciprocity including, \nbut not limited to, the date on which a background investigation is initiated, \nthe date on which the {"actor_id":"EO:13764","char_end":51715,"char_start":47207,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":10411,"char_start":9734,"text":"(a) Executive branch vetting policies and procedures relating to suitability, contractor or Federal employee fitness, eligibility to hold a sensitive position, authorization to be issued a Federal credential for access to federally controlled facilities and information systems, and eligibility for access to classified information shall be aligned using consistent standards to the extent possible, shall provide for reciprocal recognition, and shall ensure cost-effective, timely, and efficient protection of the national interest, while providing fair treatment to those upon whom the Federal Government relies to conduct our Nation's business and protect national security."},{"char_end":11078,"char_start":10851,"text":"To help fulfill these responsibilities, there shall be a primary executive branch investigative service provider whose mission is to provide effective, efficient, and secure background investigations for the Federal Government."},{"char_end":20113,"char_start":19711,"text":"\"(n) 'National Background Investigations Bureau' (NBIB) means the National Background Investigations Bureau, established within the Office of Personnel Management under section 1103(a)(3) of title 5, United States Code, or a successor entity, with responsibility for conducting effective, efficient, and secure personnel background investigations pursuant to law, rule, regulation, or Executive Order.\""},{"char_end":22855,"char_start":22190,"text":"\"(b) The aligned executive branch-wide vetting enterprise shall employ modern and consistent standards and methods, enable innovations with enterprise information technology capabilities and end-to-end automation to the extent practicable, and ensure that relevant information maintained by agencies can be accessed and shared rapidly across the executive branch, while protecting national security, protecting privacy-related information, protecting civil rights and civil liberties, ensuring resulting decisions are in the national interest and in accordance with due process requirements, and providing the Federal Government with an effective trusted workforce."},{"char_end":32056,"char_start":31684,"text":"\"(vii) shall, pursuant to section 1104 of title 5, United States Code, prescribe performance standards and a system of oversight for any suitability or fitness function delegated by the Director to the head of another agency, including uniform and consistent policies and procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, and secure completion of delegated functions."},{"char_end":33500,"char_start":33264,"text":"\"(vi) shall be responsible for developing uniform and consistent policies and procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, and secure completion of investigations and adjudications relating to eligibility for a PIV credential;"},{"char_end":37041,"char_start":36701,"text":"\"(iii) shall be responsible for developing and issuing uniform and consistent policies and procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, and secure completion of investigations, polygraphs, and adjudications relating to determinations of eligibility for access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position;"},{"char_end":40365,"char_start":40256,"text":"\"(2) provide effective, efficient, and secure personnel background investigations for the Federal Government;"},{"char_end":42890,"char_start":42694,"text":"\"(c) Delegations and designations of investigative authority in place on the date of establishment of the National Background Investigations Bureau shall remain in effect until amended or revoked."},{"char_end":44394,"char_start":43956,"text":"\"(ii) establish and maintain within as applicable, meets standards for eligibility for access to classified information or to hold a sensitive position, suitability, fitness, or credentialing, established by the respective Executive Agent;"},{"char_end":51057,"char_start":50743,"text":"\"(f) Existing delegations of authority made pursuant to Executive Order 13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, to any agency relating to granting eligibility for access to classified information shall remain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities pursuant to this order to revise or revoke such chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"SEC. 6. Policy Directives on Access, Marking, Safekeeping, Accountability, Transmission, Disposition and Destruction of Classified Information and Material. The President acting through the National Security Council shall issue directives which shall be binding on all Departments to protect classified information from loss or compromise. Such directives shall conform to the following policies:\n\n(A) No person shall be given access to classified information or material unless such person has been determined to be trustworthy and unless access to such information is necessary for the performance of his duties.\n\n(B) All classified information and material shall be appropriately and conspicuously marked to put all persons on clear notice of its classified contents.\n\n(C) Classified information and material shall be used, possessed, and stored only under conditions which will prevent access by unauthorized persons or dissemination to unauthorized persons.\n\n(D) All classified information and material disseminated outside the executive branch under Executive Order No. 10865 or otherwise shall be properly protected.\n\n(E) Appropriate accountability records for classified information shall be established and maintained and such information and material shall be protected adequately during all transmissions.\n\n(F) Classified information and material no longer needed in current working files or for reference or record purposes shall be destroyed or disposed of in accordance with the records disposal provisions contained in Chapter 33 of Title 44 of the United States Code and other applicable statutes.\n\n(G) Classified information or material shall be reviewed on a systematic basis for the purpose of accomplishing downgrading, declassification, transfer, retirement and destruction at the earliest practicable date.","sections_touched":["whole"],"signing_date":"1972-03-08","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"archival_id":"app:node/250591","filing_date":null,"grade":"mirror_transcription","instrument_id":"EO:11652","location_confidence":"medium","location_verified":false,"page_or_item":"Executive Order 11652—Classification and Declassification of National Security Information and Material; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"(v) Section 3 of Executive Order 13467 is revised to read as follows:\n\n\"Sec. 3. General Provisions. (a) Executive Order 13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, and Executive Order 10450 of April 27, 1953, as amended, are revoked. By revoking Executive Order 10450 of April 27, 1953, as amended, there is no intent to alter the requirement for an investigation for national security purposes or the \"clearly consistent with the interest of national security\" standard prescribed by that Executive Order for making the determinations referenced in section 2.7(b)(ii). Further, suitability, fitness, credentialing, and national security eligibility regulations, standards and guidance issued by, or interagency agreements entered into by, the Council, the Executive Agents, or any agency pursuant to Executive Order 10450 of\n\nApril 27, 1953, as amended, shall remain valid until superseded. Nothing in this order shall:\n\n\"(i) supersede, impede, or otherwise affect:\n\n\"(A) Executive Order 10577 of November 23, 1954, as amended;\n\n\"(B) Executive Order 12333 of December 4, 1981, as amended;\n\n\"(C) Executive Order 12829 of January 6, 1993, as amended; or\n\n\"(D) Executive Order 13526 of December 29, 2009; or\n\n\"(ii) diminish or otherwise affect the denial and revocation procedures provided to individuals covered by Executive Order 10865 of February 20, 1960, as amended; or\n\n\"(iii) be applied in such a way as to affect any administrative proceeding pending on the date of this order.\n\n\"(b) Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, is amended:\n\n\"(i) by inserting: 'Sec. 3.5. Continuous Evaluation. An individual who has been determined to be eligible for or who currently has access to classified information shall be subject to continuous evaluation as further defined by and under standards (including, but not limited to, the frequency of such evaluation) as determined by the Director of National Intelligence.'; and\n\n\"(ii) by striking 'the Security Policy Board shall make recommendations to the President through the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs' in section 6.3(a) and inserting in lieu thereof 'the Director of National Intelligence shall serve as the final authority';\n\n\"(iii) by striking 'Security Policy Board' and inserting in lieu thereof 'Security Executive Agent' in each instance;\n\n\"(iv) by striking 'the Board' in section 1.1(j) and inserting in lieu thereof 'the Security Executive Agent'; and\n\n\"(v) by inserting 'or appropriate automated procedures' in section 3.1(b) after 'by appropriately trained adjudicative personnel'.\n\n\"(c) Provisions of Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, as amended, that apply to eligibility for access to classified information shall apply to eligibility to hold any sensitive position regardless of whether that sensitive position requires access to classified information, subject to the Security Executive Agent issuing implementing or clarifying guidance regarding requirements for sensitive positions. Nothing in this order shall supersede, impede, or otherwise affect the remainder of Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, as amended.\n\n\"(d) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect the:\n\n\"(i) authority granted by law to a department or agency, or the head thereof; or\n\n\"(ii) functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.\n\n\"(e) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.\n\n\"(f) Existing delegations of authority made pursuant to Executive Order 13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, to any agency relating to granting eligibility for access to classified information shall remain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities pursuant to this order to revise or revoke such delegation.\n\n\"(g) Existing delegations of authority made by the Office of Personnel Management to any agency relating to suitability or fitness shall remain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities to revise or revoke such delegations.\n\n\"(h) If any provision of this order or the application of such provision is held to be invalid, the remainder of this order shall not be affected.\n\n\"(i) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.\"","sections_touched":["Section 3","section 2","section 6","section 1","section 3"],"signing_date":"2017-01-17","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"archival_id":"app:node/218590","filing_date":null,"grade":"mirror_transcription","instrument_id":"EO:13764","location_confidence":"medium","location_verified":false,"page_or_item":"Executive Order 13764—Amending the Civil Service Rules, Executive Order 13488, and Executive Order 13467 To Modernize the Executive Branch-Wide Governance Structure and Processes for Security Clearances, Suitability and Fitness for Employment, and Credentialing, and Related Matters; - **ACT:EO:10977>EO:13286**; Sd3145c7b44424f882132e4cb; {"actor_id":"EO:13286","char_end":40064,"char_start":39810,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":2501,"char_start":2411,"text":"Executive Order 13260 of March 19, 2002, is hereby revoked effective as of March 31, 2003."},{"char_end":41701,"char_start":40943,"text":"(a)\nin the case of the Department of Defense, the Secretary of Defense has, after consideration of the authority provided under subtitle G of title VIII of the Homeland Security Act of 2002, determined that the exercise of authority under this order is necessary for the timely and effective conduct of United States military or intelligence activities; and\n(b)\nin the case of any other executive department or agency that has authority under this order, (i) the Secretary of Homeland Security has advised whether the use of the authority provided under subtitle G of title VIII of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 would be appropriate, and (ii) the Director of the Office and Management and Budget has approved the exercise of authority under this order.\"."},{"char_end":49577,"char_start":49526,"text":"This order shall become effective on March 1, 2003."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10977>EO:13286","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. - **ACT:EO:11016>EO:12977@b7a9aeae66b2cbe2**; S59c4bfd506103502887271b6; {"actor_id":"EO:12977","char_end":45877,"char_start":45618,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":168,"char_start":0,"text":"Wanted: queue:EO:12977:Dossier gap, not a missing source: EO 13286 sec. 23 (68 FR 10619, effective 2003-03-01) amends EO 12977 secs. 1(a), 1(b), 1(c), 2, 5(a)(3) and 6."},{"char_end":1048,"char_start":703,"text":"Cited by: EO:12977\nSource: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2003-03-05/pdf/03-5343.pdf\nSHA-256 of the downloaded file: 0f74e21c46effda67c9a2824675469df809b09a321495030fa551594859554b5\nLocation: Dossier gap, not a missing source: EO 13286 sec. 23 (68 FR 10619, effective 2003-03-01) amends EO 12977 secs. 1(a), 1(b), 1(c), 2, 5(a)(3) and 6."},{"char_end":4646,"char_start":4555,"text":"Executive Order 13260 of March 19, 2002, is hereby revoked effective as \nof March 31, 2003."},{"char_end":48052,"char_start":46706,"text":"After March 1, 2003, no executive department or agency shall exercise \nauthority granted under paragraph 1A of this order with respect to any \nmatter that has been, or could be, designated by the Secretary of Homeland \nSecurity as a qualified anti-terrorism technology as defined in section 865 \nof the Homeland Security Act of 2002, unless— \n(a) in the case of the Department of Defense, the Secretary of Defense \nhas, after consideration of the authority provided under subtitle G of title \nVIII of the Homeland Security Act of 2002, determined that the exercise \nof authority under this order is necessary for the timely and effective conduct \nof United States military or intelligence activities; and \n(b) in the case of any other executive department or agency that has \nauthority under this order, (i) the Secretary of Homeland Security has advised \nwhether the use of the authority provided under subtitle G of title VIII \nVerDate Jan<31>2003 23:17 Mar 04, 2003 Jkt 200001 PO 00000 Frm 00014 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\05MRE0.SGM 05MRE0\n=== PDF page 13 of 15 ===\n10631Federal Register / Vol. 68, No. 43 / Wednesday, March 5, 2003 / Presidential Documents \nof the Homeland Security Act of 2002 would be appropriate, and (ii) the \nDirector of the Office and Management and Budget has approved the exercise \nof authority under this order.’’."},{"char_end":56608,"char_start":56557,"text":"This order shall become effective on March 1, 2003."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:11016>EO:12977@b7a9aeae66b2cbe2","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 71.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":["Without prejudice to subsections (a) through (i) of this section, all respon-\nsibilities assigned to specific Federal officials pursuant to Executive Order \n12656 that are substantially the same as any responsibility assigned to, \nor function transferred to, the Secretary of Homeland Security pursuant \nto the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (regardless of whether such responsi-\nbility or function is expressly required to be carried out through another \nofficial of the Department of Homeland Security or not pursuant to such \nAct), or intended or required to be carried out by an agency or an agency \ncomponent transferred to the Department of Homeland Security pursuant \nto such Act, are hereby reassigned to the Secretary of Homeland Security.","Executive Order 11239 of July 31, 1965 (‘‘Enforcement of the Conven-\ntion for Safety of Life at Sea, 1960 ’’), as amended, is further amended, \nVerDate Jan<31>2003 23:17 Mar 04, 2003 Jkt 200001 PO 00000 Frm 00013 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\05MRE0.SGM 05MRE0\n=== PDF page 12 of 15 ===\n10630 Federal Register / Vol. 68, No. 43 / Wednesday, March 5, 2003 / Presidential Documents \nwithout prejudice to section 1 –106 of Executive Order 12234 of September \n3, 1980 ( ‘‘Enforcement of the Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea ’’), \nby: \n(a) striking ‘‘the Secretary of Transportation ’’ in sections 1, 3, and 4, \nand inserting ‘‘the Secretary of Homeland Security ’’ in lieu thereof; and \n(b) striking ‘‘The Secretary of Transportation ’’ in sections 2 and 3 and \ninserting ‘‘The Secretary of Homeland Security’’ in lieu thereof.","Savings Provision."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"1995-10-19","target_id":"EO:11016","verb":"amend"}
  Text: [T7fb19efffd3563cd27e46dc4](#t7fb19efffd3563cd27e46dc4); absolute characters 45618–45877
